whatThisIs: The season rows of The Open Seasons Game Regulations, 2009 (Saskatchewan, c. W-13.12 Reg 3), normalised. These are DERIVED REGULATORY FACTS — dates, zones, licence classes, bag limits, animal classes — not a copy of the instrument's prose, which is what §44 permits North Ground to store with attribution. The regulation itself is not archived here; it is fetched from the King's Printer when it needs re-reading.

source.unofficialConsolidationNotice: This consolidation is not official. Amendments have been incorporated for convenience of reference and the original statutes and regulations should be consulted for all purposes of interpretation and application of the law.

howItWasProduced: Nine extraction passes over the regulation's own text, one per species group, each followed by an independent adversarial pass that re-read the source and tried to refute it. Seven groups came back with defects; every defect was in an extraction's NOTES (row tallies, a capitalisation claim, a raptor-window claim, a currency hedge) or in two fields this artefact does not rely on — `methods`, which were read off section headings and are stricter than the law, and compound park strings. No defect was found in any row's dates, licence classes, bag limits, animal classes or zones.
whatMustNotBeTrustedHere: `methods` — taken from section HEADINGS, which are not provisions. The regulation's envelopes nest (a bow is lawful in the muzzleloader season), so a builder MUST take implements from `saskatchewan-methods.ts` keyed by `seasonName` below, not from this field. The adversarial pass found this independently in three groups.

`unresolvedGeography` in the upland bird rows — empty, because the extractors were told to leave bird geography alone. A builder fills it from the Game Bird Management Unit definitions in `saskatchewan-geography.ts`.
a few compound park strings (“Saskatchewan Landing, Moose Mountain and Duck Mountain Provincial Parks”) that are verbatim source text but not atomised.
whatWasIndependentlyCrossChecked: Every row's `zones`. The 138 rows with resolvable zones were re-derived from each row's own `statedGeography` by a separate parser applying s. 3(c), and all 138 matched exactly. The only two disagreements were that parser wrongly reading “that portion of Round Lake Recreation Site lying within Wildlife Management Zone 48” as zone 48, which the extraction had correctly placed in unresolved geography — so the disagreements were the cross-check's error, not the extraction's.

The heading says 14 rows serve no zone, but the list immediately following it names 15 paragraphs, and 15 of the 53 rows do in fact carry zones: [] — 9(2.1)(b), 9(2.1)(d), 9(3)(c), 9(3)(d), 9(4)(d), 9(4)(e), 11(2.1)(d), 11(2.1)(f), 11(3)(d), 11(3)(f), 11(4)(e), 11(4)(f), 13(2.1)(e), 13(3)(d), 13(4)(e). I counted the empty-zone rows programmatically and the set matches the note's own list exactly, so only the headline number is wrong. This is a capability-reporting defect of the kind §9 forbids: a builder reconciling the unserviceable-season register against the stated 14 would either treat one real season as spurious or under-report the gap by one, and the under-report direction hides an unserviceable season rather than inventing one, so nobody would notice it.

verificationDefects.what: The documented claim about the authority's own text is false as stated: s.13 is not uniform. Two of its paragraphs use lowercase "la" and a third uses capital "La". A case-sensitive count over ss.9-13 gives 7 occurrences of "Lac La Ronge" and 2 of "Lac la Ronge"; the 7 are the 3 in s.9, the 3 in s.11, and one in s.13(4)(e). The 53 rows themselves record all three s.13 spellings correctly, so no row is defective — but the note is exactly the artefact a later normalisation pass would act on, and acting on it would silently rewrite 13(4)(e) away from what the authority published, which the extraction's own note 11 says must not happen.

verificationDefects.what: Every row omits the geography that ss. 7 and 7.1 deem open, and the notes affirmatively assert the geography inventory is complete when it is not. Elk is big game under s.2(g)(iv), so whenever an elk row opens a wildlife management zone, two protected areas and six national wildlife areas lying inside that zone are deemed open for elk by operation of law. That geography appears in no row: not in statedGeography, not in unresolvedGeography, not in extraConditions, and not in the notes' 'NOT VERIFIED HERE' list. Worse, the notes state 'GEOGRAPHY THAT CANNOT BE SERVED. Three kinds appear and all are in unresolvedGeography' and enumerate only parks/recreation sites, two partial descriptions, and Fort a la Corne WMU — a completeness claim the source refutes. The extraction cannot excuse this as out of scope, because it relies on ss. 2, 3 and 4 (equally outside ss.19-22) for the antlerless/bull definitions, for the s.3(c) suffix expansion that produced 68N/68S and 42E/42W, and for the s.4 exception that makes the five cross-year windows lawful. Having accepted that supporting provisions of the same instrument bear on the rows, it dropped the two that ADD geography. This is an understatement, which CLAUDE.md §8 treats as a false claim exactly as an overstatement is: a hunter standing in Prairie National Wildlife Area Unit 14, inside Zone 8 on 16 September, is within 22(2)(a)'s open season and this extraction would tell them nothing applies there. The fix is mechanical — one deemed-open condition attached to every zone-bearing row — and it changes no date, licence, bag or zone.

verificationDefects.what: The provenance given for the RIFLE method is fabricated, and the method is asserted on nothing the extraction actually read. The notes say: 'The RIFLE element in ss. 20 and 22 comes from "the means prescribed in The Wildlife Regulations, 1981", not from a named firearm, so the rifle entitlement is defined outside this regulation and was not verified here.' I grepped every occurrence of 'rifle' in PART III: there are exactly two, and both are section headings ('Elk archery and muzzle-loading firearm and rifle open seasons' before 20(1), and 'Elk archery and muzzle-loading firearm and rifle special open seasons' before 22(1)). The cited cross-reference says nothing about a rifle; it is an unread external instrument, so it cannot be the stated source of anything. And the headings cannot supply it either, because the same notes expressly disclaim them: 'I did not take methods from the headings alone, because in three sections the heading and the operative subsection disagree and the subsection is the rule.' So RIFLE sits in 20 rows' methods arrays supported by a heading the extraction says it did not use, under a citation to text that does not contain the word — while the one place 'rifle' genuinely appears is never cited. The method is probably correct, which is precisely the danger: a builder consuming methods would publish 'rifle permitted' as a certified legal entitlement, and an auditor tracing the stated citation would find nothing there, discrediting rows that are otherwise exact. Either cite the heading and mark the rifle entitlement UNRESOLVED pending The Wildlife Regulations, 1981, or read that regulation; do not credit a provision that does not say it.

verificationDefects.what: methods is populated as ["RIFLE"], a value taken from the section HEADING, which is not a provision. s.36(1) does not enumerate any means — it delegates them to The Wildlife Regulations, 1981. That instrument sits in the same scratchpad directory (wildlife-regs.txt) and was not read; its means regime is purely PROHIBITORY (s.17, headed "Prohibition re certain firearms") and contains no positive enumeration of permitted big-game means. A positive control confirms the grep works: that instrument mentions rifle 16 times, shotgun 9, muzzle-loading 8, crossbow 6, yet there is no "may hunt big game with" enumeration anywhere in it. Decisively, s.17(2) regulates the projectile calibre of "a shotgun or muzzle-loading rifle" used to hunt big game, which presupposes both are lawful big-game means. So the delegated set is defined by exclusion and is certainly not rifle-only. Publishing methods=["RIFLE"] asserts a restriction STRICTER than the authority — the understatement §8 forbids as squarely as a false OPEN, and the very error the extraction claims credit for avoiding in ss.31–35. The extraConditions note concedes the set "must not be published as the complete permitted-means set", which means the structured field asserts exactly what its own note denies; in a pipeline the structured field is what ships. Failure: a hunter carrying a muzzle-loading rifle or a shotgun in, say, zone 30 on 5 November is told the only legal method is a rifle, and either forgoes a lawful hunt or distrusts the product when the regulation shows otherwise. The honest encoding is an unresolved/UNKNOWN permitted-means set, not a heading-derived singleton.

verificationDefects.what: The extraction's own general-provisions block claims to carry the provisions outside ss. 37-41 that bear on these rows, and names only s. 3(b) (Central Standard Time) and s. 4 (validity of licence). It omits s. 8 "Means of hunting" — the ONLY provision anywhere in the instrument outside ss. 37-41 that speaks to these four licence classes, and one that extends WHEN their holders may lawfully hunt antlerless mule deer. I established that by sweeping the whole file rather than the sections in scope: all 24 occurrences of "Special Antlerless Mule Deer Licence" are 20 inside ss. 37-41 plus 4 inside s. 8, so s. 8 is the complete remainder and it was missed. verificationDefects.what: SHOTGUN is omitted from methods, and the reason given for omitting it does not hold. The extraction excluded shotgun because "whether a shotgun is among them" is "UNRESOLVED here and must be read from that instrument" — yet it included RIFLE from the same unread cross-reference, so identical evidence was treated two opposite ways. And the instrument is resolvable: The Wildlife Regulations, 1981 is in the same scratchpad directory (sk/wildlife-regs.txt). Its s.17 restricts rather than enumerates means — s.17(1) limits centrefire rifle cartridges, s.17(2) limits shotgun projectiles — so for big game (pronghorn, by s.2(g)(i)) both a conforming centrefire rifle and a conforming shotgun are within "the means prescribed". s.61(1) is what bars rifles, and only in the Regina-Moose Jaw and Saskatoon zones, which is precisely why s.45 covers those zones with shotgun and s.44 omits them; nothing bars a shotgun in zones 1 to 50 and 52 to 54. Omitting SHOTGUN therefore understates the lawful methods for Oct 20 to Nov 9, and section 8 is explicit that a restriction stricter than the authoritative source is a false claim just as a looser one is. verificationDefects.what: The extraction asserts the raptor window is a superset of every species season: "This window is wider than every species season in ss.46-51 and is expressly notwithstanding them, subject to the 58(3) caps." That is false for ptarmigan, and false in the dangerous direction. s.58(2) permits raptor hunting of upland game birds only from August 15 to February 28 in the following year, and is expressly "not withstanding any other provision of these regulations". s.51(2) keeps the ptarmigan season open to March 31 in the following year. Ptarmigan is an upland game bird by s.2(x), so 58(2) governs it. March 1-31 therefore falls INSIDE the ptarmigan open season but OUTSIDE the raptor window: for a raptor holder s.58(2) is a 31-day RESTRICTION on ptarmigan, not an extension. Note the grammatical ambiguity of "raptors only from August 15" does not rescue the claim - whether "only" attaches to "raptors" or to the date range, 58(2) still states February 28 as the terminal date and still overrides every other provision. The extraction already holds the contradicting fact in its own 51(2) row (crossesYear true, closesStatedAs "March 31 in the following year"), so the two rows contradict each other and the note asserts the wrong direction.

seasonsWithNoMethodEnvelope.finding: THE REGULATION RESTRICTS METHODS FOR BIG GAME AND NOT FOR UPLAND GAME BIRDS. Every big-game season section opens with a subsection naming the permitted means; the six upland bird sections (46 to 51) open with “The open seasons for X are the open seasons established pursuant to this section” and name no means at all. So a bird rule carries NO permittedImplements — unconstrained — rather than a guessed set, and `saskatchewan-methods.ts` deliberately has no entry for these six.
seasonsWithNoMethodEnvelope.theOneException: s. 58 restricts hunting upland game birds with raptors to 15 August in one year to 28 February in the following year, notwithstanding any other provision. That window is NOT a superset of every species season: ptarmigan runs 1 November to 31 March, so raptor hunting of ptarmigan is narrower at the end. The adversarial pass caught an extraction claiming the opposite, which was wrong in the permissive direction.

dateForms.finding: Dates are month and day with no year, because the seasons stand and recur until amended. Fourteen rows carry the regulation's own cross-year qualifiers instead — “December 30 in the current year”, “January 14 in the following year”, “November 1 in each year”, “August 15 in one year” — and those are kept verbatim rather than normalised, because which year a bound falls in is the fact.
